example.japanese: 今日は雨が降るかい？
example.english: Is it really going to rain today?

meaning: Something like that; similar to; in that style.

example.japanese: 猫みたいな動物がいます。
example.english: There is an animal like a cat.

distractors: ように or ような
そうに or そうな

meaning: Seeming to be; appearing to be

example.japanese: 彼は学生のようだ。
example.english: He seems to be a student.

meaning: To do something and continue into the future

example.japanese: 子どもたちは学校に行っていく。
example.english: The children will continue going to school.

example.japanese: 雨が降れば、出かけません。
example.english: If it rains, I won't go out.

example.japanese: 私は音楽を聞きながら勉強します。
example.english: I study while listening to music.

meaning: To receive someone doing something for oneself

example.japanese: 母に料理を作ってもらいました。
example.english: My mother cooked for me.

meaning: Not only ... but also; as well as

example.japanese: 彼女は日本語だけでなく英語も話せます。
example.english: She can speak not only Japanese but also English.

example.japanese: 私はあまり肉を食べない。
example.english: I don't eat much meat.

example.japanese: 日本語を勉強し始めました。
example.english: I started studying Japanese.

example.japanese: 日本語を話すことができる。
example.english: I can speak Japanese.

example.japanese: 部屋を明るくする。
example.english: Make the room brighter.

distractors: くなる or になる

example.japanese: 靴を履いたまま部屋に入らないでください。
example.english: Please don't enter the room with your shoes on.

distractors: ように or ような

example.japanese: 宿題をしなければいけない。
example.english: I have to do my homework.

pattern: ように or ような

example.japanese: 本を読むようにします。
example.english: I will try to read books.

distractors: そうに or そうな

example.japanese: こちらは新しい商品でございます。
example.english: This is a new product.

meaning: It looks like; it appears as

example.japanese: このりんごはおいしく見える。
example.english: This apple looks delicious.

distractors: そうに or そうな

meaning: a short while ago; just now

example.japanese: さっき、彼に会いました。
example.english: I met him just now.

meaning: To want someone to do something.

example.japanese: 私はあなたに来てほしい。
example.english: I want you to come.

example.japanese: これを読むか、またはあれを読むか。
example.english: Read this, or that.

example.japanese: 私は犬が好きです。
example.english: I like dogs.

meaning: To make an effort to; to ensure

example.japanese: 毎日野菜を食べるようにします。
example.english: I will make an effort to eat vegetables every day.

example.japanese: 私はこれをお持ちいたします。
example.english: I will humbly hold this for you.

example.japanese: 九時までに学校に行きます。
example.english: I will go to school by 9 o'clock.

example.japanese: りんごやバナナなどが好きです。
example.english: I like apples, bananas, etc.

example.japanese: そんなにおいしいですか？
example.english: Is it really that delicious?

example.japanese: 私はりんごとバナナを食べます。
example.english: I eat apples and bananas.

meaning: Not at all; not in the slightest

example.japanese: 全然わかりません。
example.english: I don't understand at all.

meaning: To want to; to be eager to (third person)

example.japanese: 彼は映画を見たがっています。
example.english: He seems to want to watch a movie.

distractors: がる or がっている

example.japanese: 雨が降ったら、行きません。
example.english: If it rains, I won't go.

example.japanese: 勉強し続けます。
example.english: I will continue studying.

meaning: It should be; it must be.

example.japanese: 明日、雨が降るはずだ。
example.english: It should rain tomorrow.

meaning: It cannot be; it is impossible

example.japanese: 彼が来るはずがない。
example.english: He cannot be coming.

example.japanese: 勉強してよかった。
example.english: I'm glad I studied.

distractors: てしまう or ちゃう

example.japanese: 彼は寒がりです。
example.english: He is sensitive to the cold.

distractors: がる or がっている

example.japanese: 私は勉強しなければならない。
example.english: I have to study.

meaning: To become; it has been decided that

example.japanese: 私は先生になります。
example.english: I will become a teacher.

distractors: くなる or になる

meaning: What should I do?; Is it okay if I...?

example.japanese: 駅までどうやって行ったらいいですか？
example.english: How should I get to the station?

example.japanese: 今日は雨が降るかしら。
example.english: I wonder if it will rain today.

meaning: To choose or make a decision on something.

example.japanese: コーヒーにする。
example.english: I'll have coffee.

pattern: そうに or そうな

example.japanese: 明日は雨が降りそうです。
example.english: It looks like it will rain tomorrow.

meaning: I think that; to believe that

example.japanese: 今日はいい天気だと思います。
example.english: I think the weather is nice today.

example.japanese: ぜひ来てください。
example.english: Please come, by all means.

example.japanese: 私はこっちのほうが好きです。猫より。
example.english: I like this one better than cats.

example.japanese: 私は勉強する間に音楽を聴きます。
example.english: I listen to music while studying.

example.japanese: 食べるな。
example.english: Don't eat.

example.japanese: 明日が雨なら、家にいます。
example.english: If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home.

example.japanese: ドアを開けさせてください。
example.english: Please let me open the door.

example.japanese: コンビニに行ってくる。
example.english: I will go to the convenience store and come back.

example.japanese: 私は田中という名前です。
example.english: My name is Tanaka.

example.japanese: これはおいしいではないか。
example.english: Isn't this delicious?

example.japanese: 勉強する必要がある。
example.english: It is necessary to study.

meaning: It seems like; appears to be

example.japanese: 猫みたいだ。
example.english: It seems like a cat.

example.japanese: バスは１０分おきに来ます。
example.english: The bus comes every ten minutes.

example.japanese: 宿題をやり終わった。
example.english: I finished my homework.

example.japanese: 出発したばかりです。
example.english: I just left.

meaning: It is said that; people say that

example.japanese: その山はきれいだと言われている。
example.english: It is said that the mountain is beautiful.

example.japanese: 今日、映画を見ようと思う。
example.english: I'm thinking of watching a movie today.

example.japanese: この本は小さくて読づらい。
example.english: This book is small and hard to read.

meaning: to suddenly begin or to dash out

example.japanese: ゆきがふり出した。
example.english: It started snowing.

meaning: To come; to go; to be (polite)

example.japanese: 先生はいらっしゃいますか。
example.english: Is the teacher here?

meaning: whether or not; if it is true

example.japanese: 彼が来るかどうか分かりません。
example.english: I don't know whether he will come or not.

example.japanese: きっと明日も晴れる。
example.english: Surely, it will be sunny again tomorrow.

example.japanese: 友だちが本を買ってくれる。
example.english: My friend buys a book for me.

example.japanese: 昨日、電話できなくてすみません。
example.english: Sorry for not being able to call yesterday.

distractors: てしまう or ちゃう

example.japanese: 私はりんごとかバナナとかを食べます。
example.english: I eat things like apples and bananas.

meaning: You said; he said; they said.

example.japanese: 明日行くって。
example.english: (They) said (they) will go tomorrow.

example.japanese: 今日は寒いじゃないか。
example.english: It's cold today, isn't it?

example.japanese: 早く起きなさい。
example.english: Wake up early.

example.japanese: 彼は医者だということ。
example.english: It means he is a doctor.

example.japanese: 試合の間、雨が降った。
example.english: It rained during the match.

meaning: to notice; to become aware of

example.japanese: 本に気がつく。
example.english: I notice the book.

example.japanese: 父は私に勉強させる。
example.english: My father makes me study.

example.japanese: おすしを食べてみる。
example.english: I'll try eating sushi.

distractors: てしまう or ちゃう

example.japanese: この本は読（よ）みやすいです。
example.english: This book is easy to read.

meaning: It smells; it feels; it sounds.

example.japanese: 花のにおいがする
example.english: It smells like flowers.

distractors: そうに or そうな

example.japanese: このしごとをなさいますか。
example.english: Will you do this job?

example.japanese: 天気予報によると、明日は雨らしいです。
example.english: According to the weather forecast, it seems like it will rain tomorrow.

example.japanese: 猫に魚をあげてやる。
example.english: I'll give the cat some fish.

example.japanese: 彼の優しさに感動しました。
example.english: I was moved by his kindness.

meaning: It is necessary; it is needed.

example.japanese: 水が必要だ
example.english: Water is necessary.

meaning: To have done something before; there are times when..

example.japanese: 私は日本に行ったことがある。
example.english: I have been to Japan.

example.japanese: 今日は雨が降りそうだ。
example.english: It looks like it will rain today.

example.japanese: 明日のために本を読んでおきます。
example.english: I will read the book in advance for tomorrow.

distractors: てしまう or ちゃう

example.japanese: やっと日本に行きました。
example.english: I finally went to Japan.

example.japanese: 映画は面白かったです。でも、少し長かったです。
example.english: The movie was interesting. But, it was a bit long.

example.japanese: 急に雨が降り始めました。
example.english: Suddenly, it started raining.

example.japanese: 水をください。
example.english: Please give me water.

example.japanese: 明日は雨が降るかもしれない。
example.english: It might rain tomorrow.

example.japanese: このぼうしはかみから作られています。
example.english: This hat is made from paper.

meaning: Similar to; like; in the manner of

example.japanese: かれはさるみたいにのぼります。
example.english: He climbs like a monkey.

distractors: ように or ような
そうに or そうな

example.japanese: このペンは書きにくいです。
example.english: This pen is difficult to write with.

example.japanese: 雨が降っています。それでも外に行きます。
example.english: It is raining. Even so, I am going outside.

example.japanese: 手伝っていただけませんか。
example.english: Could you please help me?

example.japanese: 雨が降っても、行きます。
example.english: Even if it rains, I will go.

meaning: You could say; it might be said

example.japanese: この本はむずかしいと言ってもいい。
example.english: You could say this book is difficult.

example.japanese: 明日買い物に行く予定だ。
example.english: I plan to go shopping tomorrow.

example.japanese: わたしも行きます。
example.english: I am also going.

example.japanese: 雨が降っているのに、サッカーをします。
example.english: Despite it raining, I will play soccer.

example.japanese: 私は友達に本を借りてあげました。
example.english: I borrowed a book for my friend.

example.japanese: 今日、雨が降るかな。
example.english: I wonder if it will rain today.

example.japanese: このケーキはおいしいし、安いです。
example.english: This cake is delicious and cheap.

example.japanese: 日本語を勉強することが好きです。
example.english: I like studying Japanese.

example.japanese: その本は読まれました。
example.english: The book was read.

meaning: To be made to do something

example.japanese: 先生に漢字を覚えさせられました。
example.english: I was made to memorize kanji by the teacher.

meaning: I heard that; I was told that

example.japanese: 彼は日本に行くと聞いた。
example.english: I heard that he is going to Japan.

meaning: I was doing; past continuous form

example.japanese: 昨日はたくさん本を読んでいた。
example.english: I was reading a lot of books yesterday.

distractors: てしまう or ちゃう

example.japanese: 私は友達にノートを取られました。
example.english: My notebook was taken by a friend.

example.japanese: 本を読んだ後で、寝ます。
example.english: After reading a book, I will sleep.

meaning: In the case of; in the event of

example.japanese: 雨の場合は、家にいます。
example.english: In the case of rain, I will stay at home.

example.japanese: こちらに本がございます。
example.english: There is a book here.

meaning: It has been decided that; it turns out that

example.japanese: 私は来年アメリカへ行くことになりました。
example.english: It has been decided that I will go to America next year.

example.japanese: 毎日ジョギングすることにします。
example.english: I will decide to jog every day.

example.japanese: 日本語がなかなか分からない。
example.english: I hardly understand Japanese.

pattern: てしまう or ちゃう
meaning: To end up doing; to do by accident

example.japanese: 宿題を忘れてしまいました。
example.english: I ended up forgetting my homework.

meaning: Not only ... but also; as well as

example.japanese: 彼女は日本語だけでなく英語も話せます。
example.english: She can speak not only Japanese but also English.

pattern: がる or がっている
meaning: To show signs of; to appear to feel

example.japanese: 彼は寒がっています。
example.english: He appears to be cold.

distractors: そうに or そうな

example.japanese: 子供の頃、よく公園であそびました。
example.english: When I was a child, I often played in the park.

example.japanese: このクラスの中で、田中さんが一番背が高いです。
example.english: Among this class, Tanaka-san is the tallest.

example.japanese: さすが、あなたはすごいですね。
example.english: As expected, you are amazing.

meaning: To reach the point where; to come to be

example.japanese: 漢字が読めるようになりました。
example.english: I have reached the point where I can read kanji.

example.japanese: 雨が降っているのに、サッカーをします。
example.english: Despite it raining, I will play soccer.

example.japanese: 映画を見よう。
example.english: Let's watch a movie.

example.japanese: 三時ごろに行きます。
example.english: I will go around 3 o'clock.
